concept.name: Best ask
concept.definition: The lowest-priced offer currently quoted for a security; at the level of a single venue it is that market's best offer, and aggregated across protected venues it forms the national best offer. Regulation NMS Rule 600(b)(15) defines best bid and best offer as the highest priced bid and the lowest priced offer.
concept.intuition: It is the least any displayed seller is currently willing to accept - the price a buyer can execute against immediately, up to the quoted size.
concept.mechanics: Sits at the top of the offer side of the order book with an associated displayed size; it moves as better offers arrive, are cancelled, or are lifted. Under Rule 600(b)(60), identical offers from different market centers are ranked by size, then by time.
concept.failure_modes: Displayed size at the best offer can be minimal or fleeting, and reserve or hidden selling interest means the effective best offer can differ from what the tape shows.
concept.misconceptions: The best ask guarantees the price only for the displayed quantity; larger buys execute through successively higher offer levels.
concept.example: Offers rest at $100.02 for 200 shares and $100.03 for 1,500 shares; the best ask is $100.02 for 200 shares only.

citations.source: 17 CFR 242.600 - NMS security designation and definitions (Regulation NMS Rule 600)
citations.section: paragraph (b)(15) Best bid and best offer
